newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump at close, hit by Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump at close, hit by Greenspan.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed down sharply on Wednesday after a mauling from bears unleashed in the wake of comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan, traders said.
"Greenspan's comments really scared the market, which had gained strongly and was ripe for profit-taking," a floor trader in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended down 48.54 points, or 1.23 percent, at 3,890.15. Trading volume was brisk at 112.5 million shares.
Traders noted that Greenspan's Senate testimony sent stock markets reeling across the world, including Wall Street.
Greenspan said, among other things, that he could not rule out increases in U.S. interest rates to contain inflationary pressure.
The Dow Jones closed off 0.78 percent at 6,983.18 points.
Telmex ADRs fell 1-1/2 to 39-1/8 on Wall Street, while its heavily weighted L shares dropped 32 centavos to 15.42 pesos. The stock accounted for 24 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Analysts noted Wednesday's fall came on the heels of three record closes in a row and they were thus not overly concerned.
"We have many reasons for saying the bourse is still a good investment option," said Roberto Garca, a fund manager at the Vector brokerage in Monterrey.
"Positive macroeconomic and microeconomic signals are luring foreign investors and many stocks are undervalued and still have upside potential to bolster the market," he added.
Technical analysts meanwhile said the bourse was taking a breather in order to consolidate recent sharp gains.

"We need to see whether the IPC respects support at 3,880 points. After that, it would define a consolidation band with a floor at 3,830," said Hctor Jimnez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
On the broad market, of a total of 122 stocks traded, decliners outweighed gainers by 77 to 19.
In percentage terms, soft-drinks bottler Gemex headed the pack with its B shares up 20 centavos at 3.50 pesos.
Another notable gainer was steemaker Hylsamex, whose B shares gained 1.20 pesos to 35.00 pesos.
Traders said the market bought Hylsamex on expectations it would post strong 1996 earnings following a favorable report on Tuesday by another steelmaker, Ahmsa.
Financial groups and blue chips topped the decliners' list .PL.MX, dealers noted.
Financial group Serfin B shares ended off 14 centavos at 3.26 pesos, while Abaco financial group's B shares fell eight centavos to 1.42 pesos.
Media group Televisa CPO shares ended off 4.90 pesos at 101.00 pesos, on the back of its ADRs, which fell 1-1/2 at 25-7/8.
((-- Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
